newsitem.title: UK: Meineke franchisor GKN stung by $398 million award.
newsitem.headline: Meineke franchisor GKN stung by $398 million award.

text.p: British vehicle components giant GKN was stung Thursday by a U.S. court verdict that awarded U.S. franchisees of the group $398 million in damages.
The sum could be raised or cut at appeal, but GKN warned that if it lost again it could suffer up to a maximum of $554 million in damages.
"We are extremely surprised at the outcome which we believe to be wholly unreasonable and will appeal following delivery of the judgment," GKN said in a statement.

It added that it would make an appropriate provision as a charge in its 1996 accounts after considering the issues in the case, which was brought by franchisees of GKN's Meineke Discount Muffler Shops Inc. in the United States.
The case was filed in December 1993 in Charlotte, North Carolina over allegations that included breach of contract over Meineke advertising.
It arose from Meineke's administration of an advertising fund to which all Meineke franchisees contribute 10 percent of their weekly revenue.

According to the American Association of Franchisees & Dealers, the fund was established in 1982 by a Meineke corporate resolution that stated that Meineke should serve only as "conduit or agent" of the advertising contributions.
However, after Meineke in 1986 set up an in-house advertising agency, New Horizons Advertising, the plaintiffs claim the firm handled funds in a way that broke that agreement.
The franchisees have said they were seeking compensatory damages in excess of $100 million, as well as punitive damages, as a result of alleged actions by New Horizons.

The Charlotte district court has already said that GKN Plc should be a defendant in the case. It also allowed part of the claim to be made under the North Carolina Unfair Trade Practices Act, which carries a triple damages penalty.
The company's shares fell sharply after the announcement, sliding 35-1/2 pence to 10.095 pounds by the close of trading.
Analysts warned that the shares could fall further if GKN failed to secure a reversal of the verdict or drastic cuts in damages.
